acceptedReports.program: Medically tailored meals, delivery and nutrition support

acceptance.scope: Independently challenged conditional health and signed recipient consumption reference; unresolved counterparty welfare, clinical utility and marginal funding remain explicit.

what: God's Love We Deliver prepares meals tailored to people living with serious illnesses and delivers them to their homes.
Registered dietitians provide nutrition care and education alongside the meals.
The organization also serves eligible children and caregivers and supports some clients transitioning to tailored groceries.
strengths: Home delivery and individualized nutrition support address difficulty shopping and cooking during serious illness.
Caregiver and child meals support the household around the ill client.
Nutrition counseling and grocery transitions offer support as clients regain the ability to prepare food.
reservations: Delivered meals and food security do not establish clinical utility gains; controlled studies give mixed results.
Contract-funded services and existing food support make the effect of another unrestricted dollar uncertain.
Clinical recipients, consumed dose and net household resources are not separately measured for the published service totals.

sections.what: God's Love We Deliver, EIN 13-3366846, provides free medically tailored meals and dietitian support. Eligibility depends on serious illness and difficulty with daily activities; income is not a universal eligibility limit. Caregivers and children are part of the delivery portfolio. [Services](https://www.glwd.org/get-meals/faqs/) New insurance pathways and grocery transitions change the service mix. [2025 operations](https://www.glwd.org/about-us/2025-impact-summary-report/)
sections.monitoring:
Controlled evidence supports nutritional and food-security outcomes more clearly than QALYs. The 2019 randomized crossover improved diet, food insecurity, reported hypoglycemia and a secondary mental-health-days measure; it did not establish persistent utility. [Original crossover](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6420590/) Maryland's pilot randomized 74 people; clinical and diabetes-quality-of-life contrasts were null, while food insecurity improved. Consumption was much lower than delivered volume. English-language, diabetes and storage requirements and disease exclusions limit transport to NYC's illness mix. [Original pilot](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11606-024-09248-x)

The 2019 instrumental-variable claims analysis and 2026 Massachusetts Medicaid matched cohort are observational. The latter's randomized comparator dates do not randomize meal receipt; its main sample requires >90 days enrollment. Neither establishes GLWD donor-level QALYs. [2019 cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6547148/) [2026 cohort](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04407-5) FAME-D's newer randomized conference abstract was found, but original full-text retrieval was blocked; no quantitative coefficient is imported. [Publisher](https://diabetesjournals.org/diabetes/article/75/Supplement_1/1249-OR/167139/1249-OR-Medically-Tailored-Meals-Lower-Hemoglobin)

Request distinct linked patients/households, consumption, service dates, controlled utility and signed household budgets. Satisfaction and payer savings are neither utility nor household income. The organization's 2025 PDF describes preliminary research and peer-reviewed work in progress; no controlled utility coefficient from those projects was established here. [Research update](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/GLWD-ImpactReport-R17-051926-1.pdf)
sections.qualitative:
Existing cash, SNAP/in-kind food, insurer meals, nonprofits and family cooking remain the baseline. Added food and freed spending form one household ledger: replaced purchases are removed, and retained consumption elsewhere is credited once. Caregiver time receives no automatic dollar value. The conditional annual ledger is $500 food consumption minus $250 substituted food plus $50 other retained consumption. Half that positive subtotal is removed for possible clinical overlap, and the full $25 burden is subtracted, giving $125 independently valued net resources. Baseline $18,000 includes existing cash and in-kind food. These are judgments, not measured GLWD effects.

A householdShare of .8 converts consumed clinical dose-years to household-year equivalents; these are not observed unique households. Insurer reimbursements fund expenses already in the denominator. Extra external/admin resources and adverse displacement are separately varied; missing fiscal costs or counterparty effects are not established zeros. Hospital savings are never deducted or converted into household resources. The central reference conditionally includes no quantified other-household displacement; this is unresolved, not a measured zero. A disjoint-household sensitivity subtracts support lost by other households at full weight. Disjoint nonconsuming delivered-dose household equivalents receive no positive consumption credit but retain full $25 receipt/storage/scheduling burdens. Thus c=0 does not imply zero household costs.
sections.cost:
Conditional full annual resources: $59,921,600.2. NYC-MSA health is 9.69 QALYs, with 4.90 signed consumption-equivalent healthy years, totaling 14.59. Main price is $41,079,886.48 per better life (ten combined equivalent healthy years); health-only is $61,865,622.21 per ten QALYs. Income equivalents are welfare comparisons, not clinical QALYs/DALYs.

A $1,000 full-resource portfolio share corresponds to 61.58 delivered meal units, 0.09 clinical delivered dose-years and 0.03 additional consumed dose-years after use and gift response. These are portfolio ratios, not a promised unrestricted-gift purchase. 520 meals is a reference service-year intensity, not a count of completed treatment or unique yearlong patients. No mortality or post-service persistence is credited.

One-year resource benefits occur at service onset. A delayed sensitivity is a new service-onset cohort and discounts both pathways at 3%; current delivered volume already reflects living recipients. Clinical-null retains $122.3 million per better life under the same resource judgment. Zero, negative and unresolved cases retain full costs and no finite positive price. Complete overlap leaves full household burdens.
sections.funding:
The current financial index links FY2024 audit and return. [Index](https://www.glwd.org/about-us/financials/) Tax functional $49,631,474 plus $10,034 COGS and $121,838 donated legal services equals audited $49,763,346. Add $2,377,336 direct event costs netted in revenue and $2,134,000 volunteer plus $199,500 advisor resources explicitly excluded from the audit: $54,474,182. An assumed 1.1 forward projection gives $59,921,600.20. Recognized donated materials/legal services are retained once. [Audit, statements and Note7](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/FY2024-Gods-Love-We-Deliver-Audited-Financial-Statements.pdf) [Return PartsVIII–IX and ScheduleD](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Gods-Love-We-Deliver-Public-Disclosure-Copy-5-15-25.pdf)

This forward resource perimeter and 2025 output are different dates, not a matched FY2025 result. FY2024 managed-care revenue is $11,583,319; donors, government and insurers continue. [Current partnerships](https://www.glwd.org/healthcare-partnerships/) No costed unrestricted incremental offer or contract substitution split was established. b=.5 is judgment. Capital/systems expansion may consume gifts before output; financing replacement makes b=0 plausible. [Donate](https://www.glwd.org/donate/) The FY2025 operating summary reports $51,256,141 expense excluding depreciation and $9,003,996 healthcare/partnership revenue. Its cost perimeter is incomplete for full resources. A separate scenario adds historical event, volunteer/advisor and depreciation proxies, without presenting them as observed FY2025 amounts. The PDF also describes a $40 million Brooklyn campaign funding infrastructure and ten years of rent, with $16 million still sought; this is concrete capital demand, not an incremental-meal offer. [2025 PDF, pages10–11](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/GLWD-ImpactReport-R17-051926-1.pdf)

model.geographicAttribution: 2025 95% five boroughs; pooled5% Hudson/Nassau/Suffolk/Westchester/Monroe. g=.975 judgment, .95–1 bounds; Monroe state unclear and MonroeNY outsideMSA.
model.formula: C=(F+E+I+L+V)*f+X; P=min(M/D,N)*r*t; E=P*c*b; Qall=E*a*u/(1+d)^delay-h; Qmsa=Qall*g. H=E*householdShare. Joint annual resource gain=(positive food net of substitution+other consumption)*distinctShare-all burdens/benefits/taxes; shared log crosswalk; W=Qmsa+I; price10=10*C/W only for W>0. Nonconsuming cohort H0=P*b*(1-c)*householdShare incurs full burden via its own disjoint log ledger; no clinical overlap haircut.
model.counterfactual: Existing insurers, public/in-kind benefits, purchased groceries, family cooking and other providers remain. a clinical nutrition substitution, b donor capacity and c consumed exposure are different steps; net financial ledger is not multiplied by a again.
model.attribution: Annual whole-recipient work with explicit donor capacity response. Meal-dose years capped at one per reported person, mixed beneficiary share adjusted; household conversion is judgment. Counseling included in utility and never stacked.
model.uncertainty: Conditional model, not empirically calibrated expectation. Consumption, household overlap, alternative food, donor response and fiscal/resource incidence unmeasured for GLWD. Missing effects are unknown, not measured causal zeros.
model.nativeOutcomes: Delivered/consumed dose-equivalent years and joint household consumption-year equivalents; no mortality/post-service credits. Clinical QALYs and signed income equivalents separate.

what: God's Love We Deliver cooks and delivers meals tailored to serious illness and provides nutrition support.
Its reported reach includes ill clients, children and caregivers, so our health model adjusts meal volume before estimating patient health.
The central model implies about $43.6 million per 10 NYC-MSA QALYs.
strengths: Concrete cooking and delivery operations reach people unable to meet nutrition needs.
Original tax reporting supports a cost denominator with direct event costs restored.
Current geographic reporting distinguishes the five boroughs from additional counties.
reservations: A recent randomized diabetes pilot improved food security but found no differential quality-of-life or clinical improvement.
Service volume includes caregivers and children and is not a count of additional clinical benefits.
Medicaid contracts and capital expansion complicate marginal unrestricted-gift allocation.

sections.what: The recipient delivers tailored meals and dietitian support to people affected by illness. A new grocery transition program and Medicaid pathways expand the service mix. This analysis prices the whole recipient against one meal-supported health pathway, with other net health provisionally zero. [Current impact](https://www.glwd.org/about-us/2025-impact-summary-report/) [Healthcare partnerships](https://www.glwd.org/healthcare-partnerships/)
sections.monitoring:
A 74-person randomized Maryland diabetes pilot used 12 meals weekly for 3 months plus dietitian calls. It reduced food insecurity, but clinical and diabetes-quality-of-life changes did not differ between arms at 6 months. This challenges translating meals into large health gains. Our 0.01 utility coefficient is a small subjective positive scenario, not a measured effect from that study; zero health remains plausible. [Original trial](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11606-024-09248-x)

Request residence, distinct clinical recipients, meals actually consumed, days exposed and controlled utility outcomes. Do not add hospitalization savings, reported satisfaction or meal counts as separate QALYs.
sections.qualitative: Home delivery may reduce physical burden and nutritional instability for people with complex illness. Alternative family support, other meal programs and insurance-funded nutrition remain available to varying degrees. Grocery transition and Medicaid expansion change the marginal service mix; it is not established that an unrestricted gift buys the historical average bundle. [Partner pathways](https://www.glwd.org/healthcare-partnerships/)
sections.cost: The model starts with FY2024 tax functional expense $49,631,474 and restores $2,377,336 direct fundraising-event costs plus $10,034 inventory cost netted outside that total, giving $52,018,844 recipient resources. A 1.1 forward multiplier gives $57,220,728.40. Benefit uses 4.2 million meals/624 meals per patient-year, 0.8 clinical-patient meal share, 0.5 incremental nutrition over alternatives, 0.01 utility gain, 0.5 gift additionality and 0.975 MSA share: 13.125 MSA QALYs. Price is $43,596,745 per 10. Exposure is volume-limited and capped at one year per client; no survival benefit or post-service continuation is credited. Volunteer time and external medical spending are excluded, so this is not full social cost effectiveness.
sections.funding:
The operating recipient's FY2024 return spans July 1, 2023–June 30, 2024. It reports $42,055,419 program, $2,084,720 management and $5,491,335 fundraising functional costs. Programs include a food festival, so food/delivery direct costs alone would understate the recipient. The same return records 4.2 million meals and 15,839 clients/caregivers/children. [Original Form 990, pages 1–2, 9–10](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Gods-Love-We-Deliver-Public-Disclosure-Copy-5-15-25.pdf)

For a $1,000 gift, scaling the whole recipient's forward cost corresponds to about 73 historical meal units before marginal-capacity and clinical adjustments; this is a portfolio equivalent, not a promised meal purchase. Public/insurance contracts and other fundraising continue; b=.5 discounts substitution. Current giving accepts ordinary gifts, with no verified restricted incremental offer. [Donation route](https://www.glwd.org/donate/)

The current 2025 impact page instead reports 3,689,816 meals and 15,115 people including children and caregivers. This model deliberately pairs FY2024 output with FY2024 expense before its assumed forward-cost multiplier; it is not a measured 2025 cost-effectiveness result. Substituting 2025 volume while retaining projected cost gives 11.530675 MSA QALYs and about $49.6 million per 10; this sensitivity does not repair the missing current expense.
